linkages: individuals in the experimental sample linked to their spouses and cohabitating partners, to check for within-family spillovers between treatment and control (456 observations, 0.107% of the sample)

sample.universe: Danish individual income tax filers; about 88% of the Danish population is liable to pay income tax and all tax liable individuals must file
sample.unit_of_observation: individual taxpayer (individual income tax return per year)
selection_rules: stratified random sample of 25,020 employees and 17,764 self-employed taxpayers (about 42,800 in total)
employees stratified by tax return complexity, with over-sampling of filers with high-complexity returns
additional stratification ensuring the same number of taxpayers from each regional tax collection agency
stage 1: random assignment to a 0% audit group or a 100% audit group for returns filed in 2007 (2006 income)

stage 2 (employees only; administratively infeasible for the self-employed): within each audit group, a third assigned a 100% threat-of-audit letter, a third a 50% letter, a third no letter, for returns filed in 2008 (2007 income)
letter analysis further restricted to employees who filed returns in both 2007 and 2008 and had an address on record so they could be reached by post
audit-effect analysis restricted to the 41,571 observations with income-change data; letter analysis to 24,788 observations
sample.period: 2006 and 2007 income years; filing and auditing seasons of 2007 and 2008
sample.n_observations: 42,784 in the experimental sample (Table A.I reports 42,778); 19,680 in the 100% audit group used for the baseline compliance analysis; 41,571 in the audit-effect analysis; 24,788 in the letter analysis

construction_notes: self-reported income is defined as total reported income minus third-party reported income, computed line by line for each taxpayer

for always-positive line items, third-party underreporting is A-F if F<A<I and I-F if F<I<=A, and zero otherwise, where I is the information report, F the filed return and A the after-audit return; self-reported underreporting is the residual

for always-negative line items (losses, deductions), underreporting is assigned to the third-party category when the item has no self-reported component and to the self-reported category when it has a significant self-reported component
the experiment measures only DETECTABLE evasion; no TCMP-style blow-up multiplier (the U.S. figure is 3.28) is applied, so all evasion estimates are lower bounds

Table II and Table III use population weights to reflect averages in the full population of Danish tax filers; Tables V, VI and A.I use experiment stratification weights, which do NOT reflect population weights

income changes in Table V are trimmed at -200,000 and +200,000 kroner, i.e. defined as min(200,000, max(income in 2007 - income in 2006, -200,000)); less than 2% of observations are trimmed on average
adjustment amounts in Table VI are capped at 10,000 kroner, affecting about 1.65% of observations for net-income adjustments and 0.75% for total tax adjustments

bunching in Table IV is defined as income within 1,500 kroner of the kink among filers within 40,000 kroner of it; the robustness column narrows the window to 20,000 kroner; incomes are grouped into 3,000 kroner bins in Figure 4
stock income of single filers is multiplied by 2 to align them with married filers, for whom the stock income tax is assessed jointly
all amounts are in Danish kroner; the paper states U.S. $1 = 5.2 DKK as of January 2010
Figure 3 restricts the sample to filers with positive income above 38,500 kroner, the tax liability threshold

the letter experiment's outcome is the difference between the prepopulated return (P) and the final filed return (F) in 2008; because 17% of taxpayers had already adjusted their return when the letters arrived, the baseline is the last return before the letters were sent

evidence.annotation: FIGURE 3.——Anatomy of tax evasion. Panel A displays the density of the ratio of evaded income to self-reported income (after audit adjustment) among those with a positive tax evasion, using the 100% audit group and population weights. Income is defined as the sum of all positive items (so that self-reported income is always positive). Panel A shows that, among evaders, the most common act is to evade all self-reported income.
